title: A Windblown Reed
subtitle: She spreads her leaves and follows the flow of air.

items.text: Reed shoots up from her seat. The storekeeper, half-startled, looks over to her.

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: What's wrong? Is that computer acting up again? Don't you worry. I'll have my daughter fix it.

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: You look a little pale. Here, have some water.
Hot steam rises up from the plastic cup.

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: These newfangled computer things are quite complex, you know. It takes time to understand how they work.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Thank you, ma'am. Can I ask, do you know of any old gates that are still around here?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Even if there's just a bit of wall left, or even a single brick! Anything!
The storekeeper looks puzzled. But eventually she gestures with her chin into the distance.

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: An old gate? You must've been too busy to notice it before. Over there.

items.speaker: Storekeeper
items.text: It's just a gate like any other. Why do you ask?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hmm.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'll have another pack of water, ma'am. Can I stay here for a couple more hours?
Even against the deep darkness, Reed can still make out the shape of the tall building.
She rubs her eyes and looks around.
Everything is still. Even the wind has stopped.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: It's late, but this must be the place. The wind's definitely slowing down around here.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: *sigh* Barbara's right. There's gotta be a reason for this interference in the network.
Reed sighs and rubs the yellowing grass on her head.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'm totally running out of time. Whoever's behind this, I gotta confront them STAT.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I guess I might miss the article deadline, but I can still solve the interface issue. That counts as a win, right?
Her grass blades sway as she watches a spider descending down a strand of web.
Reed brushes the silk with her finger.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: The wind doesn't hover in place for no reason, let alone get tangled up.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: So, if it gets tied up in a knot like this, there's gotta be some kind of special power making it stick.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: That power clings to any wind that passes by. The closer the wind is to the knot, the slower it becomes. So, all I need to do is ...

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Find the spot where the wind's moving slowest.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: *gasp* Over there!
She cries out with joy only to realize her surroundings as she ducks her head in embarrassment.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Oops, sorry. I'll try to keep it down.
Luckily, at night here in this quiet neighborhood, Reed seems to be the only one awake.
She grabs her flashlight and walks out toward the gate.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: It's close. Lemme feel for the wind again.
She reaches out her hand, but this time no silk appears.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hmm?
A breeze stirs the grass on her head.
It carries broken sobs, then the bell of an approaching bike.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I knew you'd come! C'mon! Show yourself!
Her flashlight beam sweeps the area, but it doesn't find her expected foe.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: You're OneWithFlow, right?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Wait. What if they aren't even human?
Her spirits lift a little.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I've gotta dig deeper. This'll totally make the article—

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Ah!
Something warm and heavy presses against her leg, letting out a cry like a baby.
She looks down, shocked. A bike bell rings behind her.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Alright, my bad. I shouldn't have broken into your place.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: I'll leave, I promise. Just gimme a sec.
Reed angles her flashlight downward, taking notice of a faint mark on the stone wall.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Are those carvings?

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Let me see. "Step into our gate, and gain eternity. From the hands of the immortal, law descends—no calamity, no end."

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Bingo. Finally, something concrete.
She takes a few steps forward, her left hand reaching for the spiderweb brooch on her chest.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hello? I've got some amazing findings to report. There's an old gate in town where the wind's almost totally frozen.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Hello? Barbara? Ms. Verity?
She finds a familiar silence as she nears the wall. The spider lies dormant and still.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Huh, it was pretty windy when those Carbuncles popped out. They must've disturbed the air.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Can't get any connection on the spider as is. Guess I've gotta make some wind myself.
She switches off her light.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Here goes.
She stomps her foot, and a familiar bike bell sounds nearby.
Reed silently apologizes to the small creatures.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: Next, guide the wind to untie the knot.

items.speaker: Reed
items.text: What?
Her body stiffens.
Everything vanishes. Sound, light, even smell disappear as the void swallows her whole.
Until an unfamiliar voice cuts through the darkness.
Want to try mine?
The wind sweeps her up and pulls her toward the voice, then stops and plummets.
